questions.questionTextEn: We reached the station late, and _______ missed the train.
questions.explanationEn: In the context of 'reached the station late, and _______ missed the train', an adverb modifying the verb 'missed' is required. 'Nearly' means almost, fitting the sentence naturally, whereas 'near' is an adjective/preposition.

questions.questionTextEn:
Kind : _______ : : Often : Frequently
(By word meaning)
questions.explanationEn: 'Often' and 'Frequently' are synonyms. Among the options for 'Kind', 'Mean' (Option A) is the intended answer in the initial key, though IIT Kanpur awarded Marks to All (MTA) due to ambiguity between synonym ('Type') and antonym ('Mean'/'Cruel').

questions.questionTextEn:
A series of natural numbers F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, ... obeys Fn+1 = Fn+ Fn−1
for all integers n≥2 .
If F6 = 37, and F7 = 60, then what is F1 ?
questions.explanationEn: Working backwards from F7 = 60 and F6 = 37 using Fn-1 = Fn+1 - Fn: F5 = 60 - 37 = 23, F4 = 37 - 23 = 14, F3 = 23 - 14 = 9, F2 = 14 - 9 = 5, and F1 = 9 - 5 = 4.

questions.questionTextEn:
A survey for a certain year found that 90% of pregnant women received medical
care at least once before giving birth. Of these women, 60% received medical care
from doctors, while 40% received medical care from other healthcare providers.
Given this information, which one of the following statements can be inferred with
certainty?
optionsEn: More than half of the pregnant women received medical care at least once from a doctor.
Less than half of the pregnant women received medical care at least once from a doctor.
More than half of the pregnant women received medical care at most once from a doctor.
Less than half of the pregnant women received medical care at most once from a doctor.
questions.explanationEn: Of the 90% of pregnant women who received medical care at least once, 60% received care from doctors. That amounts to 0.60 * 0.90 = 54% of all pregnant women, which is strictly more than half.

questions.questionTextEn:
Looking at the surface of a smooth 3-dimensional object from the outside, which
one of the following options is TRUE?
optionsEn: The surface of the object must be concave everywhere.
The surface of the object must be convex everywhere.
The surface of the object may be concave in some places and convex in other places.
The object can have edges, but no corners.
questions.explanationEn: A smooth 3-dimensional object (such as a torus or a dumbbell) need not be everywhere convex or everywhere concave. Its surface can be concave in some regions and convex in other regions.

questions.questionTextEn:
The country of Zombieland is in distress since more than 75% of its working
population is suffering from serious health issues. Studies conducted by competent
health experts concluded that a complete lack of physical exercise among its
working population was one of the leading causes of their health issues. As one of
the measures to address the problem, the Government of Zombieland has decided
to provide monetary incentives to those who ride bicycles to work.
Based only on the information provided above, which one of the following
statements can be logically inferred with certainty?
optionsEn: All the working population of Zombieland will henceforth ride bicycles to work.
Riding bicycles will ensure that all of the working population of Zombieland is free of health issues.
The health experts suggested to the Government of Zombieland to declare riding bicycles as mandatory.
The Government of Zombieland believes that riding bicycles is a form of physical exercise.
questions.explanationEn: Since experts identified lack of physical exercise as a leading cause of health issues and the government responded by incentivizing riding bicycles to work, the government clearly assumes that riding bicycles is a form of physical exercise.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider two functions of time (t),
f(t) = 0.01 t2
g(t) = 4 t
where 0 < t< ∞.
Now consider the following two statements:
(i)
For some t> 0, g(t) > f(t).
(ii)
There exists a T, such that f(t) > g(t) for all t> T.
Which one of the following options is TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: At t = 1, g(1) = 4 > f(1) = 0.01, so (i) holds. For t > 400, 0.01*t^2 > 4t (since 0.01*t > 4), so f(t) > g(t) for all t > T = 400, making (ii) true as well.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one of the following sentence sequences creates a coherent narrative?
(i)
Once on the terrace, on her way to her small room in the corner, she
notices the man right away.
(ii)
She begins to pant by the time she has climbed all the stairs.
(iii)
Mina has bought vegetables and rice at the market, so her bags are
heavy.
(iv)
He was leaning against the parapet, watching the traffic below.
questions.explanationEn: Mina first carries heavy bags from the market (iii), climbs the stairs and begins to pant (ii), reaches the terrace and notices the man (i), who is then described leaning against the parapet (iv). This gives the coherent sequence (iii), (ii), (i), (iv).

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following statements regarding the front-end and back-end of a
compiler.
S1: The front-end includes phases that are independent of the target hardware.
S2: The back-end includes phases that are specific to the target hardware.
S3: The back-end includes phases that are specific to the programming language
used in the source code.
Identify the CORRECT option.
optionsEn: Only S1 and S2 are TRUE.
S1, S2, and S3 are all TRUE.
Only S1 and S3 are TRUE.
questions.explanationEn: A compiler's front-end (lexical, syntax, semantic analysis, IR generation) depends on the source language and is target-independent (S1 true), while the back-end (code generation, target optimization) depends on the target hardware (S2 true) and is source-language independent (S3 false).

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one of the following sequences when stored in an array at locations
A[1], . . . , A[10] forms a max-heap?
questions.explanationEn: In a 1-indexed max-heap, every parent A[i] must satisfy A[i] >= A[2i] and A[i] >= A[2i+1]. Option (B) satisfies all parent-child constraints, whereas (A) fails at A[3]=10 < A[6]=14, (C) fails at A[5]=13 < A[10]=15, and (D) fails at A[4]=1 < A[8]=12.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let SLLdel be a function that deletes a node in a singly-linked list given a pointer
to the node and a pointer to the head of the list. Similarly, let DLLdel be another
function that deletes a node in a doubly-linked list given a pointer to the node and
a pointer to the head of the list.
Let n denote the number of nodes in each of the linked lists. Which one of the
following choices is TRUE about the worst-case time complexity of SLLdel and
DLLdel?
optionsEn: SLLdel is O(1) and DLLdel is O(n)
Both SLLdel and DLLdel are O(log(n))
Both SLLdel and DLLdel are O(1)
SLLdel is O(n) and DLLdel is O(1)
questions.explanationEn: Deleting a node given only its pointer in a singly-linked list requires finding its predecessor by traversing from head in O(n) worst-case time (unless it's not the tail and data-copy trick is disallowed/tail is deleted). In a doubly-linked list, the prev pointer is directly available, allowing O(1) deletion.

questions.questionTextEn:
The Lucas sequence Ln is defined by the recurrence relation:
Ln = Ln−1 + Ln−2,
for
n ≥3,
with L1 = 1 and L2 = 3.
Which one of the options given is TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: The characteristic equation of Ln = Ln-1 + Ln-2 is r^2 - r - 1 = 0, with roots phi = (1 + sqrt(5))/2 and psi = (1 - sqrt(5))/2. Matching L1 = 1 and L2 = 3 gives Ln = phi^n + psi^n = ((1 + sqrt(5))/2)^n + ((1 - sqrt(5))/2)^n.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one of the options given below refers to the degree (or arity) of a relation in
relational database systems?
optionsEn: Number of attributes of its relation schema.
Number of tuples stored in the relation.
Number of entries in the relation.
Number of distinct domains of its relation schema.
questions.explanationEn: In the relational database model, the degree (or arity) of a relation is defined as the number of attributes (columns) in its relation schema. The number of tuples is its cardinality.

questions.questionTextEn:
Suppose two hosts are connected by a point-to-point link and they are configured
to use Stop-and-Wait protocol for reliable data transfer. Identify in which one of
the following scenarios, the utilization of the link is the lowest.
optionsEn: Longer link length and lower transmission rate
Longer link length and higher transmission rate
Shorter link length and lower transmission rate
Shorter link length and higher transmission rate
questions.explanationEn: Stop-and-Wait utilization is U = 1 / (1 + 2a), where a = T_prop / T_trans = (length / speed) * (bandwidth / frame_size). Increasing link length and increasing transmission rate both maximize a, resulting in the lowest utilization.

questions.questionTextEn:
An algorithm has to store several keys generated by an adversary in a hash
table. The adversary is malicious who tries to maximize the number of collisions.
Let k be the number of keys, m be the number of slots in the hash table, and k > m.
Which one of the following is the best hashing strategy to counteract the adversary?
optionsEn: Division method, i.e., use the hash function h(k) = k mod m.
Multiplication method, i.e., use the hash function h(k) = ⌊m(kA −⌊kA⌋)⌋, where A is a carefully chosen constant.
If k is a prime number, use Division method. Otherwise, use Multiplication method.
questions.explanationEn: When an adversary chooses keys specifically to cause collisions against a fixed deterministic hash function, universal hashing picks a hash function uniformly at random from a universal family at runtime. This prevents the adversary from forcing worst-case collisions and guarantees O(1) expected lookup/insertion.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one or more of the following need to be saved on a context switch from one
thread (T1) of a process to another thread (T2) of the same process?
questions.explanationEn: Threads within the same process share the same virtual address space (hence the same page table base register), while each thread maintains its own execution context. Therefore, the stack pointer, program counter, and general purpose registers must be saved on a thread context switch.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one or more of the following options guarantee that a computer system will
transition from user mode to kernel mode?
questions.explanationEn: A page fault is a hardware trap handled by the OS kernel, and a system call invokes a software trap to request an OS service; both force a transition from user mode to kernel mode. A normal function call stays in user mode, and malloc() may be served from user-space heap free lists without a system call.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The intersection of two regular languages is regular.
The intersection of two context-free languages is context-free.
The intersection of two recursive languages is recursive.
The intersection of two recursively enumerable languages is recursively enumerable.
questions.explanationEn: Regular, recursive, and recursively enumerable languages are all closed under intersection (A, C, D). Context-free languages are NOT closed under intersection (e.g., {a^n b^n c^m} intersect {a^m b^n c^n} = {a^n b^n c^n} is not CFL), so (B) is false.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about
the OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocol used in the Internet?
optionsEn: OSPF implements Bellman-Ford algorithm to find shortest paths.
OSPF uses Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm to implement least-cost path routing.
OSPF is used as an inter-domain routing protocol.
questions.explanationEn: OSPF is an intra-domain (interior gateway) link-state routing protocol that uses Dijkstra's algorithm and supports hierarchical areas. Thus claiming it uses Bellman-Ford (A) or is an inter-domain protocol (C) is incorrect.

where P is a statement about integers, and Q is a statement about pairs of integers.
Which of the following (one or more) option(s) would imply Geetha’s conjecture?
questions.explanationEn: Geetha's conjecture is forall x (P(x) => exists y Q(x, y)). If forall x forall y Q(x, y) holds, the consequent is always true for any y, implying the conjecture (B). Similarly, if exists y forall x (P(x) => Q(x, y)) holds, the same witness y works for every x, which is stronger than letting y depend on x (C).

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one or more of the following CPU scheduling algorithms can potentially
cause starvation?
questions.explanationEn: Priority Scheduling and Shortest Job First can starve low-priority or long jobs indefinitely if higher-priority/shorter jobs keep arriving (C, D). Official IITK key also accepts (A, C, D) since FIFO can starve later processes if a process never yields or has infinite CPU burst.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let
f(x) = x3 + 15x2 −33x −36
be a real-valued function.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: f(x) does not have a local maximum.
f(x) does not have a local minimum.
questions.explanationEn: Taking the derivative f'(x) = 3x^2 + 30x - 33 = 3(x + 11)(x - 1) gives critical points x = -11 and x = 1. Since f''(x) = 6x + 30, f''(-11) = -36 < 0 (local maximum) and f''(1) = 36 > 0 (local minimum), so both B and D are true.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let f and g be functions of natural numbers given by f(n) = n and g(n) = n2.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: Since f(n) = n and g(n) = n^2, lim_{n->inf} f(n)/g(n) = lim_{n->inf} 1/n = 0. Therefore f grows strictly slower than g, meaning f in o(g) and consequently f in O(g).

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a 3-stage pipelined processor having a delay of 10 ns (nanoseconds),
20 ns, and 14 ns, for the first, second, and the third stages, respectively. Assume
that there is no other delay and the processor does not suffer from any pipeline
hazards. Also assume that one instruction is fetched every cycle.
The total execution time for executing 100 instructions on this processor is
ns.
questions.explanationEn: The pipeline clock cycle time is max(10, 20, 14) = 20 ns. Executing n = 100 instructions in a k = 3 stage pipeline with no hazards takes (k + n - 1) * T_clk = (3 + 100 - 1) * 20 ns = 102 * 20 = 2040 ns.

questions.questionTextEn:
A keyboard connected to a computer is used at a rate of 1 keystroke per second.
The computer system polls the keyboard every 10 ms (milli seconds) to check for
a keystroke and consumes 100 μs (micro seconds) for each poll. If it is determined
after polling that a key has been pressed, the system consumes an additional 200
μs to process the keystroke. Let T1 denote the fraction of a second spent in polling
and processing a keystroke.
In an alternative implementation, the system uses interrupts instead of polling.
An interrupt is raised for every keystroke. It takes a total of 1 ms for servicing an
interrupt and processing a keystroke. Let T2 denote the fraction of a second spent
in servicing the interrupt and processing a keystroke.
The ratio T1
is
. (Rounded offto one decimal place)
T2
questions.explanationEn: Polling every 10 ms yields 100 polls/sec, spending 100 * 100 us = 10,000 us = 10 ms, plus 200 us = 0.2 ms to process the single keystroke per second, giving T1 = 10.2 ms/s = 0.0102. Interrupt-driven I/O spends T2 = 1 ms/s = 0.001, so T1 / T2 = 10.2.

In funcp(), x is static and initialized once to 1. The first call increments it and returns 2 (main's x = 2); the second call increments it from 2 to 3 and returns 3, so y = 3 + 2 = 5 and printf prints x + y = 2 + 5 = 7.

optionsEn: f1 f2 f3 f3 f1 main f1
f1 f2 f3 f3 f2 f1
questions.explanationEn: main() calls f1(), which calls f2(2) and then f3(). f2(2) calls f3() and recursively calls f2(1) (which also calls f3() before returning 5), and finally f1()'s second direct call to f3() runs, matching the activation tree in Option (A).

The language generated by G is a∗(a + b)b∗
The language generated by G is a∗b∗(a + b)

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the IEEE-754 single precision floating point numbers
P=0xC1800000 and Q=0x3F5C2EF4.
Which one of the following corresponds to the product of these numbers
(i.e., P × Q), represented in the IEEE-754 single precision format?
questions.explanationEn: P = 0xC1800000 has sign 1 (-), biased exponent 131 (unbiased +3), and mantissa 1.0, so P = -8.0 = -2^3. Multiplying by Q = 0x3F5C2EF4 (sign 0, biased exponent 126, unbiased -1) flips the sign to 1 and adds +3 to the exponent (126 + 3 = 129), keeping the mantissa unchanged and yielding 0xC15C2EF4.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let A be a priority queue for maintaining a set of elements.
Suppose A is
implemented using a max-heap data structure. The operation Extract-Max(A)
extracts and deletes the maximum element from A. The operation Insert(A,key)
inserts a new element key in A. The properties of a max-heap are preserved at the
end of each of these operations.
When A contains n elements, which one of the following statements about the worst
case running time of these two operations is TRUE?
optionsEn: Both Extract-Max(A) and Insert(A,key) run in O(1).
Both Extract-Max(A) and Insert(A,key) run in O(log(n)).
Extract-Max(A) runs in O(1) whereas Insert(A,key) runs in O(n).
Extract-Max(A) runs in O(1) whereas Insert(A,key) runs in O(log(n)).
questions.explanationEn: In a binary max-heap with n elements, its height is O(log n). Extract-Max removes the root and sifts down in O(log n) worst-case time, and Insert appends at the end and sifts up in O(log n) worst-case time.

foo() computes and prints the sum of values in each subtree in post-order (left, right, root). For the given tree: leaf 3 prints 3, leaf 8 prints 8, node 5 prints 5+3+8 = 16, leaf 13 prints 13, node 11 prints 11+13 = 24, and root 10 prints 10+16+24 = 50, giving '3 8 16 13 24 50'.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let U = {1, 2, . . . , n}, where n is a large positive integer greater than 1000. Let
k be a positive integer less than n. Let A, B be subsets of U with |A| = |B| = k
and A ∩B = ∅. We say that a permutation of U separates A from B if one of the
following is true.
- All members of A appear in the permutation before any of the members of B.
- All members of B appear in the permutation before any of the members of A.
How many permutations of U separate A from B?
questions.explanationEn: Choose 2k positions out of n for the elements of A union B in C(n, 2k) ways, and arrange the remaining n - 2k elements in (n - 2k)! ways. In those 2k positions, either all of A occupy the first k positions and B the last k, or vice versa (2 choices), with k! arrangements each, giving 2 * C(n, 2k) * (n - 2k)! * (k!)^2.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let f : A →B be an onto (or surjective) function, where A and B are nonempty
sets. Define an equivalence relation ∼on the set A as
a1 ∼a2 if f(a1) = f(a2) ,
where a1, a2 ∈A. Let E = {[x] : x ∈A} be the set of all the equivalence classes
under ∼. Define a new mapping F : E →B as
F([x]) = f(x),
for all the equivalence classes [x] in E.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: F is an onto (or surjective) function.
F is a one-to-one (or injective) function.
questions.explanationEn: If [x1] = [x2], then f(x1) = f(x2), so F([x]) = f(x) is well-defined (A false). Since f is onto B, F is onto (B); since F([x1]) = F([x2]) implies x1 ~ x2 and [x1] = [x2], F is one-to-one (C), and therefore F is a bijection (D).

questions.questionTextEn:
Suppose you are asked to design a new reliable byte-stream transport protocol
like TCP. This protocol, named myTCP, runs over a 100 Mbps network with Round
Trip Time of 150 milliseconds and the maximum segment lifetime of 2 minutes.
Which of the following is/are valid lengths of the Sequence Number field in the
myTCP header?
questions.explanationEn: At 100 Mbps = 12.5 * 10^6 B/s over MSL = 120 s, up to 1.5 * 10^9 bytes can be transmitted before wrap-around. Since 2^30 = 1.07 * 10^9 < 1.5 * 10^9 <= 2^31, at least 31 bits are needed, making 32, 34, and 36 bits valid lengths.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let X be a set and 2X denote the powerset of X.
Define a binary operation Δ on 2X as follows:
AΔB = (A −B) ∪(B −A) .
Let H = (2X, Δ). Which of the following statements about H is/are correct?
optionsEn: Every element in H has an inverse, but H is NOT a group.
For every A ∈2X, the inverse of A is the complement of A.
For every A ∈2X, the inverse of A is A.
questions.explanationEn: Symmetric difference Delta on the powerset 2^X is associative, commutative, has the empty set as identity, and satisfies A Delta A = empty set for every A in 2^X. Thus H is a group (A) and every element is its own inverse (D).

questions.questionTextEn:
Suppose in a web browser, you click on the www.gate-2023.in URL. The browser
cache is empty. The IP address for this URL is not cached in your local host, so
a DNS lookup is triggered (by the local DNS server deployed on your local host)
over the 3-tier DNS hierarchy in an iterative mode. No resource records are cached
anywhere across all DNS servers.
Let RTT denote the round trip time between your local host and DNS servers
in the DNS hierarchy. The round trip time between the local host and the web
server hosting www.gate-2023.in is also equal to RTT. The HTML file associated
with the URL is small enough to have negligible transmission time and negligible
rendering time by your web browser, which references 10 equally small objects on
the same web server.
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT about the minimum elapsed
time between clicking on the URL and your browser fully rendering it?
optionsEn: 7 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.
5 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
9 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.
6 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
questions.explanationEn: Iterative lookup over the 3-tier DNS hierarchy takes 3 RTTs, and fetching the base HTML takes 1 RTT (TCP) + 1 RTT (GET) = 2 RTTs. With persistent HTTP and pipelining, all 10 objects arrive in 1 more RTT (total 6 RTTs, D); with non-persistent HTTP and 5 parallel TCP connections, 2 batches of 5 objects take 2 * 2 = 4 RTTs (total 9 RTTs, C).

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a random experiment where two fair coins are tossed. Let A be the event
that denotes HEAD on both the throws, B be the event that denotes HEAD on
the first throw, and C be the event that denotes HEAD on the second throw.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: The first and second coin tosses are independent, so B and C are independent (C) and consequently P(B|C) = P(B) (D). However, A = B intersect C has P(A) = 1/4 while P(A|B) = 1/2 != 1/4, so A is dependent on both B and C.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider functions Function 1 and Function 2 expressed in pseudocode as
follows:
Function 1
Function 2
while n > 1 do
for i = 1 to 100 ∗n do
for i = 1 to n do
x = x + 1;
end for
x = x + 1;
end for
n = ⌊n/2⌋;
end while
Let f1(n) and f2(n) denote the number of times the statement “x = x + 1” is
executed in Function 1 and Function 2, respectively.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: In Function 1, the inner loop runs n + floor(n/2) + floor(n/4) + ... <= 2n times, so f1(n) = Theta(n) and f1(n) in O(n) (D). Function 2 executes the statement exactly 100n = Theta(n) times, so f1(n) in Theta(f2(n)) (A).

questions.questionTextEn:
Let G be a simple, finite, undirected graph with vertex set {v1, . . . , vn}. Let Δ(G)
denote the maximum degree of G and let N = {1, 2, . . .} denote the set of all possible
colors. Color the vertices of G using the following greedy strategy:
for i = 1, . . . , n
color(vi) ←min{j ∈N :
no neighbour of vi is colored j}
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: This procedure results in a proper vertex coloring of G.
The number of colors used is at most Δ(G) + 1.
The number of colors used is at most Δ(G).
The number of colors used is equal to the chromatic number of G.
questions.explanationEn: Greedy coloring assigns each vertex a color distinct from all already-colored neighbors, always yielding a proper vertex coloring (A). Because each vertex has at most Delta(G) neighbors, at least one color in {1, ..., Delta(G) + 1} is always available, bounding the colors used by Delta(G) + 1 (B).

questions.questionTextEn:
Let U = {1, 2, 3}. Let 2U denote the powerset of U. Consider an undirected graph
G whose vertex set is 2U. For any A, B ∈2U, (A, B) is an edge in G if and only
if (i) A̸ = B, and (ii) either A ⊊B or B ⊊A. For any vertex A in G, the set of
all possible orderings in which the vertices of G can be visited in a Breadth First
Search (BFS) starting from A is denoted by B(A).
If ∅denotes the empty set, then the cardinality of B(∅) is
.
questions.explanationEn: Because the empty set is a proper subset of every non-empty subset in 2^U, it is adjacent to all 7 other vertices in G. Therefore, a BFS starting at empty set discovers all 7 vertices at level 1 and can visit them in any of the 7! = 5040 permutations.

The 128 x 128 array has 16,384 integers, occupying 16,384 / 512 = 32 pages (each row of 128 ints is 1/4 of a page, so 4 rows fit per page). Since the loop accesses column-by-column across all 32 pages sequentially with only 30 frames under LRU, every access to a new page evicts the oldest page; each of the 128 columns touches all 32 pages, causing 128 * 32 = 4096 page faults.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a computer system with 57-bit virtual addressing using multi-level
tree-structured page tables with L levels for virtual to physical address translation.
The page size is 4 KB (1 KB = 1024 B) and a page table entry at any of the levels
occupies 8 bytes.
The value of L is
.
questions.explanationEn: With 4 KB = 2^12 byte pages, the page offset is 12 bits, leaving 57 - 12 = 45 bits for virtual page indexing. Each page holds 4096 / 8 = 512 = 2^9 PTEs (9 bits per level), so L = 45 / 9 = 5 levels are required.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a sequence a of elements a0 = 1, a1 = 5, a2 = 7, a3 = 8, a4 = 9, and
a5 = 2. The following operations are performed on a stack S and a queue Q, both
of which are initially empty.
I: push the elements of a from a0 to a5 in that order into S.
II: enqueue the elements of a from a0 to a5 in that order into Q.
III: pop an element from S.
IV: dequeue an element from Q.
V: pop an element from S.
VI: dequeue an element from Q.
VII: dequeue an element from Q and push the same element into S.
VIII: Repeat operation VII three times.
IX: pop an element from S.
X: pop an element from S.
The top element of S after executing the above operations is
.
questions.explanationEn: After I & II: S (top->bottom) = [2,9,8,7,5,1], Q (front->rear) = [1,5,7,8,9,2]. After III–VI (2 pops from S, 2 dequeues from Q): S = [8,7,5,1], Q = [7,8,9,2]. Operations VII–VIII dequeue 7, 8, 9, 2 and push them onto S giving S = [2,9,8,7,8,7,5,1], and IX–X pop 2 and 9, leaving 8 at the top of S.

Consider a database of fixed-length records, stored as an ordered file. The database
has 25,000 records, with each record being 100 bytes, of which the primary key
occupies 15 bytes. The data file is block-aligned in that each data record is fully
contained within a block. The database is indexed by a primary index file, which
is also stored as a block-aligned ordered file. The figure below depicts this indexing
scheme.

Suppose the block size of the file system is 1024 bytes, and a pointer to a block
occupies 5 bytes. The system uses binary search on the index file to search for a
record with a given key. You may assume that a binary search on an index file of
b blocks takes ⌈log2 b⌉block accesses in the worst case.
Given a key, the number of block accesses required to identify the block in the data
file that may contain a record with the key, in the worst case, is
.
questions.explanationEn: Each data block holds floor(1024 / 100) = 10 records, so 25,000 records span 25,000 / 10 = 2,500 data blocks, giving 2,500 primary index entries. Each index entry is 15 + 5 = 20 bytes, so each index block holds floor(1024 / 20) = 51 entries, requiring ceil(2500 / 51) = 50 index blocks. Binary search on 50 index blocks takes ceil(log2(50)) = 6 block accesses.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the language L over the alphabet {0, 1}, given below:
L = {w ∈{0, 1}∗| w does not contain three or more consecutive 1’s}.
The minimum number of states in a Deterministic Finite-State Automaton (DFA)
for L is
.
questions.explanationEn: To reject strings with three or more consecutive 1's, the DFA needs to track the length of the current trailing run of 1's: 0 ones (q0), 1 one (q1), 2 ones (q2)—all accepting—plus a non-accepting trap state q3 for >= 3 consecutive 1's. Thus the minimal DFA has 4 states.

questions.questionTextEn:
An 8-way set associative cache of size 64 KB (1 KB = 1024 bytes) is used in a
system with 32-bit address. The address is sub-divided into TAG, INDEX, and
BLOCK OFFSET.
The number of bits in the TAG is
.
questions.explanationEn: In a 64 KB = 2^16 byte, 8-way set-associative cache, each way has size 64 KB / 8 = 8 KB = 2^13 bytes. Regardless of block size, the combined (INDEX + BLOCK OFFSET) bits equal log2(8 KB) = 13 bits, leaving 32 - 13 = 19 bits for the TAG field.
